items.title: Saturday snapshot: flu and RSV still lead the board — and the Children's Hospital wait is much shorter this morning
items.body:
No new provincial report has landed since BCCDC's Nov 12 summary and Fraser Health's Nov 12 outbreak bulletin, so the big picture is unchanged: flu season is early and still climbing in B.C.

One detail worth knowing if your family visits grandparents in care: the Vancouver Sun reported Nov 13 that Vancouver Coastal Health's outbreak bulletin lists five flu outbreaks — four at care homes and one at a hospital in Sechelt. That is on top of the 12 influenza outbreaks at Fraser Health long-term care homes we counted on Fraser Health's own page, plus COVID-19 outbreaks at three Fraser Health hospitals, the newest declared Nov 11 at Burnaby Hospital. Fraser Health asks anyone with a cough, fever or flu-like symptoms to please not visit care facilities right now.

Today's snapshot from our live board: Influenza A and RSV both rank High and Rising at the top, Influenza B is High, and everyday cold viruses (entero/rhinovirus) are still High but falling; COVID-19 is High and falling too.

The calmer news is at the ER door: BC Children's Hospital's posted wait was about 2 hours 15 minutes at our check this morning, down a lot from about 6 hours 30 minutes yesterday afternoon. Waits swing through the day, so check the live board before heading out — and for non-urgent worries, HealthLink BC at 811 can help you decide where to go; for a true emergency, call 911.

It is a rainy indoor-play kind of Saturday (9–11°C, air quality low risk). Simple habits help most right now: wash hands often, keep kids home with a fever or a new cough, and let a sick-day care-home visit wait for a video call instead.

items.title: Federal data now puts B.C. in the 'high' flu category — and flu outbreaks are hitting Lower Mainland care homes
items.body:
New federal numbers reported today (Nov 13) raise the flag a notch higher than this morning's provincial update. Health Canada says flu activity is rising across the country and is expected to keep trending upward in the coming weeks, with B.C. — along with Alberta, Prince Edward Island and the Yukon — seeing a high percentage of tests coming back positive. The Vancouver Sun, reporting on the same federal data, puts B.C.'s flu test positivity at public health laboratories at 17.8 to 27.4 per cent, with only Nunavut higher.

Why does BCCDC call B.C. flu 'moderate' while the federal scale says 'high'? The two agencies use different yardsticks — PHAC itself notes federal and provincial activity levels are expected to differ. The direction both point to is the same: flu is climbing, and earlier than usual.

You can see it in care homes, too. Fraser Health's outbreak bulletin, last updated Nov 12, lists 12 active influenza outbreaks at long-term care homes across the region, declared between Oct 23 and Nov 10 — plus COVID-19 outbreaks at three hospitals. Fraser Health asks anyone with a cough, fever or flu-like symptoms to please not visit care facilities right now. If your kids have grandparents in care, a sick-day visit can wait — a video call is the safer hello this week.

This afternoon's snapshot from our live board: Influenza A ranks High and Rising, and RSV has moved up to High and Rising as well. The posted ER wait at BC Children's Hospital was about 6 hours 30 minutes at our last check this afternoon, up from about 3 hours 30 minutes this morning — waits swing a lot, so check the live board before heading out. For non-urgent worries, an urgent and primary care centre or HealthLink BC at 811 can help you decide; for a true emergency, call 911.

One practical note: flu shots are free in B.C. for everyone 6 months and older, and kids under 9 who have never had a flu shot need two doses, at least four weeks apart — so starting this week still leaves time to get both in before the holidays.

items.title: BCCDC's Nov 12 update: flu is moderate, RSV is still low — but kids' respiratory visits are ticking up
items.body:
BCCDC's newest weekly summary, published Nov 12, says influenza test positivity in BC is at moderate levels, and flu indicators across Canada were moderate and increasing in the most recent reporting week.

RSV is still quiet for now — test positivity remains low and wastewater levels are stable and low — while COVID-19 test positivity is low-to-moderate, wastewater levels are moderate-to-high at most sites, and hospital admissions have stayed low in recent weeks.

One note for parents: BCCDC says emergency department and primary care visits for respiratory illness are still at low levels overall, but there have been recent increases among children.

Today's snapshot from our live board: COVID-19 and Influenza A rank High in our BC wastewater ranking, RSV is marked Rising, and Influenza B is Low; this morning, BC Children's Hospital's posted ER wait was about 3 hours 30 minutes.

A season reminder: flu and COVID vaccines are available in BC at no cost for everyone 6 months and older, and if your child is not in urgent trouble, HealthLink BC at 811 can help you decide where to go.

BCCDC's latest weekly summary (Nov 5) puts influenza activity in BC at moderate, and provincial testing suggests flu is picking up earlier than usual this season — most flu detections so far are influenza A (H1N1). COVID-19 activity across BC is low-to-moderate, and RSV is still low for now.

The germ showing up most often in recent BCCDC sentinel swabs is none of those — it's the everyday cold viruses (entero/rhinovirus), ahead of flu. In LittleBuggy's own Metro Vancouver wastewater snapshot, COVID-19 and Influenza A currently rank High, while RSV is Low but rising: the season is warming up, not peaking.

Some calmer news on measles: the Public Health Agency of Canada declared the countrywide measles outbreak over on Oct 19, and BCCDC reports no measles cases in BC since May. Travel-related cases can still appear, so keeping kids' vaccinations up to date still matters. This season's flu and COVID vaccines are now open in BC for everyone 6 months and older, at no cost.

Today's snapshot from our live board: the posted ER wait at BC Children's Hospital this afternoon was about 4 hours. If your child isn't in urgent trouble, an urgent and primary care centre or HealthLink BC at 811 can save you a long night.
items.title: Flu is arriving early in BC — and plain old colds are still beating everything else
